# Active priority — screenshot failures, then supported-title PSE Bank features

Every confirmed user-submitted PSE Bank screenshot failure is resolved by a concrete code change and recorded successful automatic Android compile. Continue one bounded PSE Bank feature across supported game titles per valid new successful Slack validation event. Any new user-submitted screenshot failure takes priority over this feature sequence.

## Scope extension — add Generations 8 and 9 PSE Bank transfers

Continue the existing Gen 1–7 transfer repair and route-matrix work, and extend usable individual-Pokémon PSE Bank transfers through Generations 8 and 9 under the same criteria. Keep this separate from unrelated Switch save editing.

Repository inventory confirms native Switch Bank deposit and restore adapters exist for Sword/Shield (PK8), Brilliant Diamond/Shining Pearl (PB8), Legends: Arceus (PA8), Scarlet/Violet (PK9), and Legends: Z-A (PA9). The title-level converter route inventory also names these games, but that inventory alone does not mean a reviewed cross-generation conversion is implemented. Add and connect the actual source/destination conversion adapters and Bank UI for each supported title; do not treat PK8, PB8, PA8, PK9, or PA9 as interchangeable formats.

For every newly enabled route, use the existing transfer criteria: preserve the source save and Bank record until the native destination write and reopen verification succeed; show the exact transformed, omitted, or user-selected Legalise fields; write one explicitly chosen empty native slot; update only the required Pokédex flags and checksums; retain and verify a recovery backup; and restore both sides on failure. Block unsupported mappings instead of silently discarding fields. Backward routes are PSE conversions and make no official-trade or verified-provenance claim.

After the active Gen 1–7 recovery issue is resolved, begin the forward extension with Gen 7 → Gen 8, implementing title-specific destination paths for Sword/Shield, BDSP, and Legends: Arceus. Continue with Gen 8 → Gen 9 and Gen 7 → Gen 9 for Scarlet/Violet and Legends: Z-A only where exact destination-valid mappings are supported. Then expand the directional matrix using the same route review and rollback requirements.


Switch feature work is paused. Maintain and repair individual-Pokémon PSE Bank transfers for supported saves in Generations 1–7. Do not regress existing working routes or describe conversions as official in-game trades. Transfers must run through PSE Bank, preserve the Bank record until the native destination write and reopen verification succeed, preserve existing destination contents, and keep source saves unchanged.

Current bounded issues from the 8 November transfer video and attached Bank screenshot: Gen 4 → Gen 3 rejects a Gen 4-origin record (the shown Origin Game ID is 7). Keep the default strict block for unsupported records, but offer an explicit Legalise choice of one of the five Gen 3 origin titles, disclose that provenance changes and PK3 met location becomes unspecified (0), and preserve the Bank record until destination persistence and reopen verification succeed. This does not certify legality or history. Existing supported Pal Park records retain their source Gen 3 title. The later 8 November screenshots also show: Gen 3 → Gen 4 rejects a PK3 ability flag that conflicts with PID parity; add an explicit PID Legalise choice that preserves the saved ability slot, nature, gender and shiny state, disclose the PID change, and block PID-dependent forms/evolution outcomes that cannot be preserved. Gen 5 → Gen 4 rejects Origin Game ID 23; offer an explicit pre-Gen-5 origin ID mapping and disclose the provenance edit. Gen 6 ↔ Gen 7 rejects origin IDs 35 and 33; allow a user-selected Gen 6 origin ID in the converted native record, disclose that history is unverified, and retain the existing Bank/destination rollback and reopen protections. Other bounded issues from the video: (1) Gen 3 → Gen 4 can reject valid ability slots when remote historical metadata omits them; use PSE's canonical Gen 3 ability data and keep exact ability checks. (2) Gen 4 → Gen 5 rejects slot 2 when a species has only one non-hidden ability; map that sole ability for either PID parity. (3) Gen 4 and Gen 5 derive normal ability slots from different PID bits, so Gen 4 ↔ Gen 5 conversions must remap PID only when required and disclose it in the preview. Preserve the actual ability, nature, shiny state, TID/SID, and exact Bank record; only perform a deterministic PID change that satisfies the destination format and preserves shiny/nature constraints. Keep blocking hidden abilities and ambiguous multi-ability mappings. Preserve all destination contents outside the selected slot and existing checksum, backup, native write, reopen verification, source preservation and rollback behavior. Continue preserving the delivered Gen 3 → Gen 2 conversion disclosure.

## User screenshot issues — main-series Bank transfer repairs (2026-11-16)

Work on the active `pse-phone-auto-v2-test` branch of the public repository. Preserve the current safety model: never silently rewrite provenance, drop or replace moves, normalize forms, overwrite occupied destination slots, or remove a Bank record before the native destination has been written and reopened successfully. Keep explicit Legalise choices visible and cancellable, bind source and destination snapshots, and retain rollback/recovery behavior. No test or build work is requested in this feature-first phase.

1. **Gen 6 → Gen 4 and Gen 6 → Gen 3 origin Legalise preflight — resolved and automatically validated.** Both routes offer a destination-valid, cancellable origin choice when the source origin cannot be represented. They pass the explicit rewrite state through the Generation 5 bridge preflight and build the bridge with the reviewed destination origin; otherwise the bridge keeps strict origin validation. The source Bank record and destination remain bound and unchanged through preparation.
